key_insight: PI-MFA reconstructs continuous flow fields with B-splines while enforcing governing physics, so the approximation stays both smooth and physically consistent.
engineering_relevance: This is useful for downstream differentiation, visualization, and analysis of flow data when measurements or simulations are low-fidelity or physically inconsistent.
method: Tensor-product B-splines provide compact, continuously differentiable flow representations.
Control points are optimized to balance data fidelity with PDE residuals plus initial and boundary conditions.
Exact analytical spline derivatives make residual evaluation efficient without storing full-resolution fields.
evidence_signal: Across 1D convection-diffusion, 2D coupled Burgers, and 2D incompressible Navier-Stokes tests, PI-MFA reduced PDE residuals and improved global balance-law consistency, often with lower approximation error than standard or regularized MFA.
watch_item: Performance depends on choosing appropriate PDE constraints and optimization settings, so mismatched physics models or weak boundary/initial data could limit reconstruction quality.
paper_title: A Physics-Informed B-Spline Framework for Continuous Approximation of Flow Data
